# `silk/crypto/curve448`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Agree on a shared secret with X448 (RFC 7748), and sign with Ed448 (RFC 8032), on the Goldilocks
curve, Curve448.

## When to use
Use [`X448`](#X448) when two parties must get the same secret over a channel that others can read and
a 224-bit security level is wanted, for example in a TLS 1.3 handshake with the `x448` group.
Each side makes a key with [`X448.generate`](#X448.impl.generate), sends [`X448.publicKey`](#X448.impl.publicKey), and calls
[`X448.agree`](#X448.impl.agree) with the public key of the other side. Then derive the real keys from the shared
secret with `silk.crypto.hkdf`. Use [`Ed448PrivateKey`](#Ed448PrivateKey) to sign and [`Ed448PublicKey`](#Ed448PublicKey) to verify
Ed448 signatures, with a context or prehashed (Ed448ph) when the protocol asks for it. For the
more common 128-bit level, use `silk.crypto.x25519` and `silk.crypto.ed25519`.

## Details
X448 secrets, public keys, and shared secrets are 56 bytes, little-endian. A secret is clamped as
RFC 7748 says, so all 56-byte values are valid. Ed448 seeds and public keys are 57 bytes, and
signatures 114 bytes. The field is the integers modulo `p = 2^448 - 2^224 - 1`, held as eight
56-bit limbs, and every step on a secret runs in constant time. Nothing allocates. Use
`silk.crypto.okp_key` to read and write the keys in PKCS #8 and SubjectPublicKeyInfo.

## Errors
- [`X448Error`](#X448Error) for an input with the wrong length, or for a peer key that gives an all-zero
  secret.
- [`Ed448Error`](#Ed448Error) for a seed, key, or signature of the wrong length, a key that is not a point, a
  signature that does not verify, or a context longer than 255 bytes.

## Gotchas
The exchange does not tell you who the other side is. An attacker in the middle can run one
exchange with each side. Authenticate the exchange, for example with a certificate signature. Do
not use the shared secret directly as a key. Keys are not erased when they are dropped. Ed448,
Ed448 with a context, and Ed448ph signatures do not verify as each other.

## Examples
### Agree on a secret (RFC 7748 test vector)
```silk
import silk.core.result { Result }
import silk.crypto.curve448 { X448, X448Error }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  // Real programs use `X448.generate()` with a secure `Random` provider.
  let alice = match X448.fromSecret(
    b"\x9a\x8f\x49\x25\xd1\x51\x9f\x57\x75\xcf\x46\xb0\x4b\x58\x00\xd4\xee\x9e\xe8\xba\xe8\xbc\x55\x65\xd4\x98\xc2\x8d\xd9\xc9\xba\xf5\x74\xa9\x41\x97\x44\x89\x73\x91\x00\x63\x82\xa6\xf1\x27\xab\x1d\x9a\xc2\xd8\xc0\xa5\x98\x72\x6b"
  ) {
    Result<X448, X448Error>.Success { value } => move value
    Result<X448, X448Error>.Failure { error: _ } => {
      return 1
    }
  }
  let bob = match X448.fromSecret(
    b"\x1c\x30\x6a\x7a\xc2\xa0\xe2\xe0\x99\x0b\x29\x44\x70\xcb\xa3\x39\xe6\x45\x37\x72\xb0\x75\x81\x1d\x8f\xad\x0d\x1d\x69\x27\xc1\x20\xbb\x5e\xe8\x97\x2b\x0d\x3e\x21\x37\x4c\x9c\x92\x1b\x09\xd1\xb0\x36\x6f\x10\xb6\x51\x73\x99\x2d"
  ) {
    Result<X448, X448Error>.Success { value } => move value
    Result<X448, X448Error>.Failure { error: _ } => {
      return 1
    }
  }
  let alicePublic = X448.publicKey(&alice)
  let bobPublic = X448.publicKey(&bob)
  let fromAlice = match X448.agree(move alice, &bobPublic) {
    Result<[u8; 56], X448Error>.Success { value } => value
    Result<[u8; 56], X448Error>.Failure { error: _ } => {
      return 1
    }
  }
  let fromBob = match X448.agree(move bob, &alicePublic) {
    Result<[u8; 56], X448Error>.Success { value } => value
    Result<[u8; 56], X448Error>.Failure { error: _ } => {
      return 1
    }
  }

  // Both sides get 07fff418...a5d.
  if alicePublic[0] != 0x9b || fromAlice[0] != 0x07 || fromBob[0] != 0x07 || fromBob[55] != 0x5d {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

<a id="X448"></a>

## `X448`

```silk
pub struct X448
```

An X448 key pair: a secret and its public key.

### When to use
Use it when two parties must get the same secret over a channel that others can read. Each side
makes a key with [`X448.generate`](#X448.impl.generate), sends [`X448.publicKey`](#X448.impl.publicKey), and calls [`X448.agree`](#X448.impl.agree) with the
public key of the other side.

### Details
[`X448.agree`](#X448.impl.agree) consumes it; [`X448.agreeWith`](#X448.impl.agreeWith) borrows it, for a static key. Secrets, public
keys, and shared secrets are 56 bytes, little-endian. Nothing allocates.

### Gotchas
The exchange does not tell you who the other side is. Authenticate the exchange, for example
with a certificate signature. Derive the real keys from the shared secret with
`silk.crypto.hkdf`. The key is not erased when it is dropped.

```silk
impl X448
```

<a id="X448.impl.fromSecret"></a>

### Associated function `fromSecret`

```silk
pub fn fromSecret(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<X448, X448Error>
```

Returns the key pair for the 56-byte secret `bytes`. The bytes are copied, and clamped as RFC
7748 says before use.

#### Errors
- `InvalidScalarLength` if `bytes` is not 56 bytes.

#### Gotchas
For a new exchange, use [`X448.generate`](#X448.impl.generate). A secret that is used for two exchanges gives the
same public key to both, so the exchanges can be linked.

<a id="X448.impl.generate"></a>

### Associated function `generate`

```silk
pub effect fn generate() -> X448 ? &mut Random
```

Returns a new key pair with a secret from 56 bytes of the ambient `Random`.

The `Random` provider must be cryptographically secure. If it fails, the program stops. There
is no fallback to a weaker source.

<a id="X448.impl.secret"></a>

### Method `secret`

```silk
pub fn secret(self: &X448) -> [u8; 56]
```

Returns the 56 secret bytes as they were given, before clamping. PKCS #8 stores these bytes.

<a id="X448.impl.publicKey"></a>

### Method `publicKey`

```silk
pub fn publicKey(self: &X448) -> [u8; 56]
```

Returns the 56-byte public key to send to the peer. It does not consume the key pair.

<a id="X448.impl.agree"></a>

### Method `agree`

```silk
pub fn agree(self: X448, peer: &[u8]) -> Result<[u8; 56], X448Error>
```

Returns the 56-byte shared secret for the public key `peer` of the other side, and consumes
the key pair.

As RFC 7748 says, any 56-byte value is accepted, also a value that is not below `p` or a point
that is not on the curve.

#### Errors
- `InvalidPeerLength` if `peer` is not 56 bytes.
- `AllZeroSharedSecret` if the result is all zeros. Stop the exchange.

The key pair is consumed also when it fails.

<a id="X448.impl.agreeWith"></a>

### Method `agreeWith`

```silk
pub fn agreeWith(self: &X448, peer: &[u8]) -> Result<[u8; 56], X448Error>
```

Returns the 56-byte shared secret for the public key `peer`, as [`X448.agree`](#X448.impl.agree) does, but
borrows the key pair so that a static key can agree with many peers.

#### Errors
- `InvalidPeerLength` if `peer` is not 56 bytes.
- `AllZeroSharedSecret` if the result is all zeros. Stop the exchange.

#### Gotchas
A static key gives no forward secrecy. Prefer a new key pair for each exchange.

<a id="Ed448PrivateKey"></a>

## `Ed448PrivateKey`

```silk
pub struct Ed448PrivateKey
```

An Ed448 private key that signs messages (RFC 8032 section 5.2).

### When to use
Make it from a 57-byte seed with [`Ed448PrivateKey.fromSeed`](#Ed448PrivateKey.impl.fromSeed), or make a new one with
[`Ed448PrivateKey.generate`](#Ed448PrivateKey.impl.generate). Then call [`Ed448PrivateKey.sign`](#Ed448PrivateKey.impl.sign). Use
[`Ed448PrivateKey.signWithContext`](#Ed448PrivateKey.impl.signWithContext) when the protocol names a context, and
[`Ed448PrivateKey.signPrehashed`](#Ed448PrivateKey.impl.signPrehashed) for Ed448ph.

### Details
The seed is what RFC 8032 calls the private key, and what PKCS #8 stores for Ed448. The key
keeps the seed, the clamped secret scalar, the nonce prefix, and the public key. Signing is
deterministic and runs in constant time for the secret values.

### Gotchas
Secrets are not erased.


Returns the 114-byte Ed448 signature of `message` with an empty context, `R` followed by

<a id="Ed448PrivateKey.impl.signWithContext"></a>


Returns the Ed448 signature of `message` with `context`, which binds the signature to one use.

#### Errors

<a id="Ed448PrivateKey.impl.signPrehashed"></a>

### Method `signPrehashed`

```silk
pub fn signPrehashed(self: &Self, message: &[u8], context: &[u8]) -> Result<[u8; 114], Ed448Error>
```

Returns the Ed448ph signature of `message` with `context`: the signature of the 64-byte
SHAKE256 hash of `message`, marked as prehashed.

#### Errors
`ContextTooLong` when `context` is longer than 255 bytes.

#### Gotchas
Ed448ph signatures do not verify as Ed448 signatures, and the other way round.

<a id="Ed448PublicKey"></a>

## `Ed448PublicKey`

```silk
pub struct Ed448PublicKey
```

A decoded Ed448 public key, for signature verification (RFC 8032 section 5.2).

### When to use
Use it to check that a message was signed by the holder of a known Ed448 key. Decode the key
once with [`Ed448PublicKey.fromBytes`](#Ed448PublicKey.impl.fromBytes), then call [`Ed448PublicKey.verify`](#Ed448PublicKey.impl.verify).

### Details
Verification requires the scalar half of the signature to be below the group order, and checks
that `[S]B - [k]A` encodes to `R`, as OpenSSL does. It works on public data and does not try to
run in constant time. It does not allocate.
